scenes.say: Plasma is the liquid portion of blood. It normally makes up a little over half its volume and carries dissolved substances. An erythrocyte, or red blood cell, contains haemoglobin. That protein binds oxygen at the lungs and releases it in tissues.
Platelets are small cell fragments circulating in the blood. At an injury they stick to the damaged vessel and to each other, forming a plug.
Fibrin strands form a mesh at the injury. They reinforce the platelet plug and trap blood cells to produce a more stable clot.
JAMB asks which component forms most of the volume, which cell carries oxygen, and which fragments initiate a clot. Blue arrows trace oxygen entering a red cell or platelets moving to injury.

quickCheck.prompt: Which blood component first forms a plug in a damaged vessel?
quickCheck.feedback: Platelets adhere and aggregate. Fibrin later strengthens the plug.
